slides.title: Do your blade ends have to be rounded?
slides.sub: Yes. Check all four in two minutes

slides.title: The rule is exact
slides.body: ISU Communication No. 2636 says tubes must be closed and blade ends rounded to a minimum radius of 10 mm. No points at either end of either blade.

slides.title: Use a 20 mm circle
slides.body: A 10 mm radius is the curve of a 20 mm circle. If the tip curves tighter than that circle, the end needs shaping.

slides.title: Square corner or rounded end
slides.caption: Judge the end profile from the side, at the front and back of both blades.

slides.title: Check all four ends
slides.body: Front and back, left and right, with cut resistant gloves on. A tip that met a kerb, a bench or another skate is usually the odd one out.

slides.title: Shape the ends, never the middle
slides.body: Clamp the blade in a jig and follow the curve with short strokes of a bench stone. Your rocker, bend and edges live on the running surface. Leave it.

slides.text: Four ends, a 20 mm circle, two minutes.
